title: Article 127 — Appointment of ad hoc Judges

content.overview: Article 127 provides that if at any time there is a lack of quorum of the Judges of the Supreme Court available to hold or continue any session, the Chief Justice of India may, with the previous consent of the President and after consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned, request in writing a Judge of a High Court who is duly qualified for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court to sit and act as an ad hoc Judge of the Supreme Court for such period as may be necessary. While so sitting and acting, the Judge has all the jurisdiction, powers and privileges of a Supreme Court Judge and is bound by the duties of such a Judge.
content.glance: Lack of SC quorum: CJI (with President’s consent; after consulting HC CJ) may request a qualified HC Judge to sit as ad hoc SC Judge.
content.study:
Article 127 ad hoc Judges:
- Trigger: lack of quorum of SC Judges to hold or continue a session.
- Process: CJI requests in writing, with previous consent of the President, after consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned.
- Who: a High Court Judge duly qualified for appointment as an SC Judge.
- Effect: full jurisdiction, powers, privileges and duties of an SC Judge while sitting and acting.

Examination: quorum gap; CJI request; President’s consent; consultation with HC CJ; qualification for SC appointment.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Trigger: insufficient SC Judges for quorum.
2. CJI requests in writing with previous consent of President, after consulting the CJ of the High Court concerned.
3. Appointee: HC Judge qualified for SC appointment.
4. While acting: full powers and duties of an SC Judge.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When may ad hoc Judges of the Supreme Court be appointed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 127, if there is a lack of quorum of Supreme Court Judges to hold or continue any session, the Chief Justice of India may, with the previous consent of the President and after consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned, request a High Court Judge who is duly qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge to sit and act as an ad hoc Judge of the Supreme Court for the necessary period.

examTips: Quorum gap; CJI + President consent + HC CJ consultation; qualified HC Judge.

keyTakeaways: Art 127: ad hoc SC Judges from High Courts when quorum lacking.
